data.title: Homepage
data.hero_sub: Falling in love with Lake Tahoe is easy. Buying well in a market of about 10,000 parcels, where one street changes the value and one winter changes the neighborhood, takes an agent who has watched it since 1992.
data.reality_heading: Incline Village Isn't Like Any Market You've Bought In Before.
data.reality_body: Grant C. Meyer works only in Incline Village and Crystal Bay, a micro market that doesn't follow the trends in Reno, the Bay Area, or even Truckee. Values can change across one street, and a thousand feet of elevation means five times the snow load. Our team reads this market for buyers and sellers, on their side of the table.
data.stat1_desc: More closed sales in Incline Village than any other agent since January 1, 2019, per Incline Village MLS data.
data.stat2_desc: Sellers here expect a cash offer. A local lender and a clean contract are what let the other 40% compete.
data.stat3_desc: About 700 agents work in one small town, and Grant knows most of them. Knowing what the other side needs is how offers get accepted here.
data.cta_heading: Every Tahoe Story Starts With One Conversation.
data.cta_body: Buying, selling, or curious what your place is worth? Call or text the team line, and one of us picks up.
data.emotion_h1: Are You Coming to Ski, to Retire, or to Raise a Family?
data.emotion_body: It is the first question Grant asks every buyer, before bedrooms, views, or price. The answer decides the neighborhood, the elevation, the walk to the beach, and whether a condo or a house makes sense.
data.proof_body: One client has completed 23 transactions with our team. Many of the sellers we list have bought or sold with Grant before, and several came to us this year after a year with another agent and no sale.
data.micro_heading: Same Zip Code, Very Different Markets
data.insights_body: Notes from inside the market: what's selling, what's stalling, and why the answer changes with the elevation.

data.title: Buyers
data.lead: Many of the most significant properties in Incline Village never see a public listing. Grant's network surfaces them first.
data.card1_p: Direct access to properties before they hit Compass or MLS — from generational lakefront homes to ski-in mountain estates.
data.card2_p: Buyer agency that prioritizes your privacy. NDA-backed showings, blind offers when appropriate.
data.card3_p: Tahoe-specific zoning, water-rights, and TRPA permitting handled before they become deal-killers.
data.card4_p: We help with property managers, contractors, IVGID enrollment, and the hundred small things between purchase and possession.
data.headline: Quiet Access to Tahoe's Most Coveted Estates.

data.title: Sellers
data.lead: Selling Tahoe property is personal. Our process is tailored for sellers who care as much about who buys it as what it sells for.
data.card1_p: Off-market positioning that protects your privacy and the property's storyline.
data.card2_p: Selective staging, photography, and a calibrated price ladder — built around comparable transactions, not algorithms.
data.card3_p: Cash-pre-approval verification, intentions discussion, and lifestyle-fit conversations before a single showing.
data.card4_p: Coldwell Banker Global Luxury network places your home in front of the right buyers in Aspen, Jackson, and Park City.
data.headline: A Sale Designed Around Your Life, Not Just the Listing.

data.title: Concierge
data.lead: Our work doesn't stop at the closing table. Call the team about anything the house needs, and we will either handle it ourselves or find the person who will.
data.card1_p: Movers, utilities, the storage unit key, and a welcome dinner when you arrive. We have even parked a client's Rivian in a garage for him.
data.card2_p: Plumbers, electricians, the boiler specialist, the mold crew, and the handyman who will pick up after the dog. Years of knowing who shows up.
data.card3_p: Establishing Nevada residency is a specialty in itself. We connect you with local CPAs who handle it every day, with any conflicts disclosed up front.
data.card4_p: Snow season, roof shoveling, landscaping, and a set of eyes on the house between visits, from the same people we trust with our own homes.
data.headline: Nothing Is Too Big or Too Small.

data.title: About
data.lead: From a 16-year-old part-time ski instructor at Diamond Peak to one of the most consistently top-ranked Sierra agents, Grant has built his career on a single bet: that knowing your client matters more than knowing the market.
data.card1_p: Born in Reno. Family moved to Incline in 1989. Helped run his grandfather's small fly-fishing outfit on the East Shore — that's where the relationships started.
data.card2_p: JD from McGeorge School of Law, real-estate-focused. Practiced for four years before moving into agency in 2007.
data.card3_p: "You don't sell Tahoe by selling Tahoe. You sell it by listening for what someone is actually looking for, and then quietly finding it."
data.card4_p: Coldwell Banker International Society of Excellence, six consecutive years. Top 1% of Sierra agents by volume.
data.headline: Three Decades. One Lake. Thousands of Conversations.

data.title: Crystal Bay
data.blurb: The state-line gateway, where grand lakefront estates meet original mid-century cabins on wooded lots.
data.hero_sub: The state-line gateway, where grand lakefront estates meet original mid-century cabins on wooded lots.
data.overview: Crystal Bay sits where Highway 28 crosses from California into Nevada, wrapping the northwest corner of the lake. It's the quieter, more weathered cousin of Incline Village — a mix of grand lakefront estates and original mid-century cabins on wooded lots, many held by the same families for generations.
data.take: Crystal Bay rewards patience. The lakefront here rarely lists publicly, and when it does the right buyer is often already on a list. If this is the corner you want, the move is to be known here before the home exists.

data.title: Community Page
data.hero_sub: Grant C. Meyer has called Incline Village home since 1992 and is raising his family here. These are the neighborhoods, the beaches, the schools, and the history as a resident knows them, with the homes for sale in each one.
data.nb_intro: Tap an area on the map to see its character, or pick a neighborhood below. Each opens its own guide, with the homes currently for sale there.
data.todo_heading: What Living on the North Shore Looks Like
data.todo_intro: Skiing in the morning and the beach by afternoon. The calendar here runs on the seasons.
data.todo1_p: A community-owned ski resort with some of the best lake-view runs on the North Shore, and short lift lines compared with the bigger Tahoe resorts.
data.todo2_p: Incline, Burnt Cedar, and Ski Beach are reserved for residents and their guests, with swimming, picnics, and boat access through the summer.
data.todo3_p: The Robert Trent Jones championship course and the shorter mountain course, both run by the community improvement district.
data.todo4_p: Hiking and biking from the village down to the lake, plus the East Shore Trail and Sand Harbor's coves just off Highway 28.
data.todo5_p: Boating, paddleboarding, and kayaking on the clearest large lake in the country, with full-service marinas a short drive away.
data.todo6_p: Captain Whittell's stone lakeside castle south of Sand Harbor, open for docent-led tours through the summer months.
data.quote_text: This is where I live and have lived for a long time. So I want clients to know that this is my community too.
data.quote_cite: Grant C. Meyer · Incline Village since 1992
data.schools_heading: Learning, a Few Minutes From Home
data.schools_body: Incline Village built its first elementary school in 1964, and its high school followed as the community took shape. Today, families choose between the local public schools and a handful of private options, all within the village.
data.school2: Private K–8 options within the village
data.school3: A newer elementary campus completed in 2009
data.history_heading: From Logging Camp to Master-Planned Village
data.h1_p: The North Shore began as timber country, feeding the Comstock silver mines of Virginia City. Through the 1800s, a narrow-gauge line hauled logs up the mountain to a V-flume, and the scars of that era still trace the ridgelines between Mill Creek and Sand Harbor.
data.h2_p: By the early 1900s, the lake had become a summer escape. Captain George Whittell bought some 40,000 acres and built a stone castle south of Sand Harbor, the Thunderbird Lodge, where he was known for lavish parties and a private menagerie that included lions and an elephant.
data.h3_p: In the 1960s, the Crystal Bay Development Company acquired Whittell's holdings and set out to build a master-planned community. Robert Trent Jones designed the golf course, the name Incline Village was chosen, and the first school opened in 1964, setting the framework of the village you see today.
data.living_intro: The practical side of the move: how you get here, what residency opens up, and what the year feels like.
data.live1_p:
Reno–Tahoe International Airport sits about 45 minutes down Highway 431, which makes Incline Village one of the more reachable luxury markets in the Sierra.

Sacramento and the Bay Area are an easy weekend drive, and most of the village is only a few minutes from Highway 28 along the shore.
data.live2_p:
The Incline Village General Improvement District runs the private beaches, Diamond Peak, both golf courses, the tennis complex, and the recreation center.

Access comes through an annual recreation fee billed with your Washoe County property taxes, one of the things that makes residency here distinct.
data.live3_p:
Incline sits between roughly 6,225 and 7,700 feet, which gives it four real seasons: deep, snowy winters and dry, mild summers, with around 290 days of sunshine a year.

Snow piles up through the winter, well over a hundred inches in a typical year, then gives way to long, clear summers on the lake.
data.live4_p:
The village covers the basics close to home: Raley's and the Village shopping center for groceries, the recreation center and library at the core, and the public and private schools, all within a few minutes.

For specialized care and bigger errands, Tahoe Forest Health System is over the hill in Truckee, and Reno's hospitals and shopping are about 45 minutes away.

data.title: About
data.hero_headline:
You've Found the Place.
Now Find the Right Guide.
data.hero_sub: Since 2019, Grant C. Meyer has closed more sales in Incline Village than any other agent, with nearly $500 million in career sales. He and his team work only in Incline Village and Crystal Bay, the town he has called home since 1992.
data.why_body: Incline Village and Crystal Bay form a micro market of about 10,000 parcels, where two or three new listings can change what a home is worth. After the winter of 2022–23, the biggest Grant has seen, high-elevation owners listed all at once and values there fell, while neighborhoods a few miles lower climbed. Knowledge like that comes from watching this market since 1992.
data.why_quote: I can't be an expert in all those markets and I'm not. I'm only an expert in mine.
data.stat1_desc: Career sales volume in Incline Village and Crystal Bay.
data.stat2_desc: 181 closed sales in Incline Village since January 1, 2019, the most of any agent in the MLS. In 2025, Grant led the market in both units and dollar volume.
data.stat3_desc: Real estate is Grant's full-time profession, and his four-person team covers every day of the week.
data.guide_heading: Home Since 1992. Still the First to Answer the Phone.
data.cred1_d: Arrived in eighth grade. College, law school, and a stint in the Caribbean took him away, and he always came back.
data.cred2_d: JD and MS programs at Vermont Law School. Grant is not an attorney, but he brings that training to every contract and land-use question.
data.cred3_d: Son of a local general contractor and engineer, raised on job sites. He reads a home's construction as closely as its price.
data.cred4_d: President, Incline Village REALTORS, 2023. Realtor of the Year, 2024. President-Elect, Nevada REALTORS, 2026.
data.guide_body: Grant learned client service in his family's restaurants. His parents owned two pizza restaurants in Lake Tahoe, and Grant ran them as COO before the family sold them and he left for law school. The family business taught him to earn a customer the first time, so he never has to earn them again.
data.guide_body2: Grant runs a relationship-based business. Many clients buy and sell with him again, and one has completed 23 transactions with the team, netting more than $5 million in profit.
data.guide_quote: No matter where life takes you, it's hard to beat Incline Village. Something about this place always brings you back.
data.pillars_heading: Three Challenges Unique to This Market.
data.pillar1_challenge: A micro market of about 10,000 parcels. Two identical floor plans a street apart can sell for very different prices, and one big winter can send an entire elevation band to market at once. Online estimates are notoriously inaccurate here.
data.pillar1_cred: Grant prices every home against the current competition, meaning the listings buyers can tour today, as well as recent sales. In a market where two or three new listings can move a home's value, recent sales alone usually miss it.
data.pillar2_challenge: Impervious coverage, BMP requirements, and TRPA rules exist nowhere else in Nevada. The contract has its own traps, including when a contingency waives itself and when earnest money becomes non-refundable.
data.pillar2_cred: Grant reviews the purchase agreement clause by clause with every client, so you know which terms protect you and which protect the other side.
data.pillar3_challenge: An accepted offer only puts you at the 50-yard line. Inspections, appraisal, repairs, and title still stand between you and the keys, and the best local contractors are booked for months.
data.pillar3_cred: We advocate for our clients through closing, with trades, inspectors, and local lenders we have worked with since 2009. On one sale, mold found at the last minute nearly ended the deal. Our specialist treated it within 90 minutes, and the sale closed two days later.
data.proof_heading: Nothing Too Big or Too Small.
data.proof1_story: A client ran out of gas in the middle of Mount Rose Highway. Grant drove up with a five-gallon drum in his Tesla, a car that has never had a drop of gas in it. In his words, “that's what you do.”
data.proof2_story: Before one showing, the team arranged movers and packed a client's closet of designer handbags into a storage unit. Grant met the movers for the key and put it in the client's hand himself.
data.proof_transition: Our team provides full concierge service, and we will either handle a request ourselves or find the right person for it. We pride ourselves on responding to every phone call, text, and email as soon as possible.
data.return_heading: When You Buy Here, You're Not a Visitor Anymore.
data.return_body: College at USC, law school in Vermont, a stint as a scuba divemaster in the Caribbean, and a few years near family each took Grant away from Incline Village, and each time he came back. He and his wife have been back full-time for about 17 years, raising their two daughters in the town where he grew up. In 2023, Grant served as President of Incline Village REALTORS. He was named Incline Village Realtor of the Year in 2024 and is President-Elect of Nevada REALTORS for 2026.

data.title: Buyers
data.hero_headline: Find Your Place on the North Shore.
data.hero_sub: Are you coming to ski, to retire, to raise a family, or to establish Nevada residency? It is the first question Grant asks, because the answer shapes every decision after it. Start there, and our team will show you how this market really works.
data.stakes_heading: Out-of-Market Instincts Cost Real Money Here.
data.stakes_p1: Incline Village and Crystal Bay don't behave like most markets, where an online estimate lands close to the truth and a confident buyer can handle a purchase alone.
data.stakes_punch: Here, that confidence can be expensive.
data.stakes_p2: In 2021, a buyer paid $3.88 million for a home bought directly from the owner, with no agent on either side. Two years later, they listed it. The home took three and a half years to sell and closed at $1.92 million, less than half of what they paid.
data.stakes_p3: This is a micro market of about 10,000 parcels, and a handful of sales can move it. The same floor plan can sell for a very different price one street over, and one hard winter can send a whole elevation band to market at once.
data.stakes_quote: You can avoid making those 50, 60% mistakes by paying 3 to 6%. In our market, it's a fantastic insurance policy to hire a professional.
data.network_heading: The Network You Inherit on Day One.
data.network_p1: This is a resort market. There's no Home Depot in Incline Village, the best contractors are booked for months, and the right specialist is hard to find unless you already know who to call.
data.network_p2: Since 2009, Grant has sent steady work to the trades, lenders, title officers, inspectors, and appraisers who do it right, and treated them well, so they pick up when we call. In a small town, reputations travel fast, and we know which specialists show up. Our clients inherit that network the day they close.
data.network_story: A buyer's inspector flagged mold at the last minute, and the buyer was ready to walk. Our mold specialist was treating the house within 90 minutes, and the sale closed two days later.
data.network_quote: My business and the way I work, relationships are everything to me.
data.tax_body: Nevada is one of the most tax-friendly states in the country. The state charges no personal income tax or business tax, capital gains aren't taxed at the state level, and property taxes stay low because Nevada doesn't reassess to your purchase price the way most states do. For buyers coming from California, and lately from Washington, crossing the state line can change the financial picture as much as the house does.
data.tax_turn: What that means for you depends on why you're moving.
data.tax1_kicker: Retiring here, or planning your estate
data.tax1_title: Keep what you spent a career building.
data.tax1_body:
Nevada charges no personal income tax. Your pension, 401(k) withdrawals, Social Security, and investment income keep their full value at the state level.

There's also no state estate or inheritance tax. When you pass your home and assets to your children or grandchildren, Nevada takes none of it. (Federal estate tax rules still apply, so your estate planner is still worth a call.)

For anyone who spent a career building wealth, that combination is the difference between preserving an estate and watching it shrink a little more every year.
data.tax2_kicker: Earning at the top of your career
data.tax2_title: Income earned as a resident is not taxed by the state.
data.tax2_body:
A high salary or a strong year of capital gains lands very differently here. Against California's top rate, the gap is large enough to factor into where you choose to live.

The part worth understanding: the benefit follows residency, not the deed. To claim it, you make Nevada your true home, where you live, vote, and spend your time. Plenty of people make exactly that move to Incline Village, and a local CPA can walk you through what genuine residency requires.
data.tax3_title: A structure built to keep overhead low.
data.tax3_body: Nevada earned its business-friendly reputation, and the structure backs it up:
data.tax3_bullets:
No corporate income tax
No franchise tax
No gross receipts tax for most businesses (a Commerce Tax applies only above $4M in Nevada revenue)
No inventory tax
Strong legal protection for company directors and officers
A high degree of privacy for business owners
data.tax3_after: For an entrepreneur relocating a company, or running one from a home office above the lake, those add up to lower overhead and fewer state-level headaches. Whether to restructure an entity in Nevada is a decision for your CPA and attorney, and our team can introduce you to local professionals who handle it.
data.tax4_title: Low property taxes, and one fee that opens the lake.
data.tax4_body:
Property taxes in Nevada are low by national standards, and well below what most of our buyers leave behind. Nevada also doesn't reassess to your purchase price, so the bill stays low long after you close.

Incline Village is an unincorporated community of Washoe County. Water and sewer service, the private beaches, Diamond Peak Ski Resort, the championship golf courses, the tennis complex, and the recreation center are all managed by the Incline Village General Improvement District (IVGID). Every parcel comes with recreation privileges, which is the closest thing to a country club membership that arrives with the deed.
data.tax_disclaimer: This is general information, not tax or legal advice, and every situation is different. Before you count on any of it, sit down with a local CPA. Grant refers clients to Ashley Quinn CPAs in Incline Village, who specialize in establishing Nevada residency. In full disclosure, the firm also prepares Grant's own personal and business taxes.
data.investment_heading: Your Home Here Is Also a Portfolio Decision.
data.investment_p1: Almost every buyer we work with treats a purchase here as an investment, even when it is the home they plan to raise a family in. One client has completed 23 transactions with our team, buying about a dozen properties, selling a dozen, keeping one, and netting more than $5 million along the way.
data.investment_p2: Most buyers here want turnkey, remodeled homes, and those sell at a premium. That leaves real equity for the buyer willing to take on a project with the right guidance. Grant grew up on his father's job sites, so he can spot good bones and estimate what a remodel will really cost. Plan on construction here running about 50% longer and 50% more expensive than you budget for, and on some streets returning every dollar while others never will.
data.investment_quote: Most of my clients are just as smart, if not smarter than I am. If I can provide them the right information, they usually make the right decisions.
data.comm_heading: Two Communities, Known Block by Block.
data.comm_lead: Incline Village and Crystal Bay each have their own character, pricing, and quirks. The sun in February, the walk to dinner, the months of shoveling: all of it changes by neighborhood, and Grant's notes on each are on the community pages.
data.comm1_desc: The beaches, Diamond Peak, the golf and tennis, and subdivisions Grant has watched trade since 1992. Even across one street, values can be very different.
data.comm2_desc: Quieter, more wooded, right at the state line, with its own pricing logic, from the lakefront to the hillside lots.
data.process_heading: What Working With Our Team Looks Like.
data.process_body: The first call covers what you plan to do here, how you will use the property, and whether you are paying cash or financing. Many of our buyers come from out of the area, so the next step is learning the town: the neighborhoods, what a thousand feet of elevation does to a winter, what each parcel's IVGID recreation privileges include, and the Nevada tax picture.
data.process_promise: When you're ready, we show you the current competition, not just what sold six months ago, because in a micro market that is what sets the price. We call the listing agent before we write, to learn what matters to their seller, so the offer can win on terms that cost you nothing. An accepted offer is the 50-yard line. From there we handle inspections at whatever depth you want, a local lender for the 40% of buyers who finance, the appraisal, repairs, title, and the utilities and movers.
data.cta_heading: Ready to Buy in Tahoe the Right Way?
data.cta_body: Reaching out commits you to nothing. The first conversation covers your goals, your timeline, and whether Tahoe is the right move. Call or text the team line, and one of the four of us picks up.
data.stakes_p4: Knowledge like that doesn't live in a database. Grant has watched this market since 1992, and our team reads it for you, on your side of the table.
data.process_body2: We look online first. Then you come up, and we caravan past the schools, the ball fields, and the restaurants you can walk to from one street but not the next. Some buyers decide in a weekend and some take years, and we keep sending listings either way.

data.title: Sellers
data.hero_headline: Your Home's Value Here Isn't What an Algorithm Says It Is.
data.hero_sub: In the most desirable neighborhoods here, an original 1962 house can sit next door to brand-new construction, and the algorithm averages them. That is why online estimates are notoriously inaccurate in this town. Since 2019, Grant has closed more sales in Incline Village than any other agent, and he prices against what buyers can tour today.
data.pricing_heading: The Hardest Number to Get Right in This Market.
data.pricing_p1: Grant starts where an appraiser would, with price per square foot and what closed in the last six months. Then he adds what many agents skip: the current competition, meaning what a buyer for your type of property has on the shelf right now. Six new listings below you can make last spring's comps irrelevant, while nothing on the market within $200,000 of you can mean room to price higher.
data.pricing_p2: Online estimates get this town wrong for a specific reason. Most markets value by proximity, and here proximity means little. An original 1962 home and new construction can share a lot line, so the algorithm overvalues one and undervalues the other.
data.pricing_p3: Our job is to give you what we know. You make the call. Some sellers need to close this season, and some are happy to wait years for their number. Grant will tell you honestly which price gets which result.
data.pricing_quote: The market will tell us whether we're priced right or not.
data.timing_heading: The Sellers Who Win Here Are Ready Before the Buyers Arrive.
data.timing_p1: Buyers usually arrive before sellers are ready. They come up to ski in the winter and start looking in April and May, while many owners are still in Arizona, Las Vegas, or Palm Springs and haven't been up to get the house ready for summer.
data.timing_p2: So we list earlier in the spring than most, and we sell many homes before the competition arrives. In one recent mild winter, we brought new listings on in November, when most agents had pulled theirs in October, and drew full-price, all-cash, multiple offers.
data.timing_p3: Our team brought a remodeled three-bedroom condo to market in early spring and set the complex record at $715,000. By late summer, the neighbors who saw that number had listed, and Grant found a different client a nicer three-bedroom in the same complex for $100,000 less. Same building, months apart, and our clients were on the right side of both.
data.timing_quote: Usually buyers are here before sellers are ready, so we have started putting our listings on the market earlier in the spring than most.
data.mkt_heading: Every Listing Gets the Full Package, Whatever the Price.
data.mkt_p1: Every listing gets professional photography, drone, video, and its own property website, whatever the price point. Most of our buyers see a home first on a screen from hundreds of miles away, and that first look has to be its best.
data.mkt_p2: Before the camera arrives, our stager sets the home up to show at its best. Then the property gets a champagne brunch broker tour for the 700 agents in town, open houses, and a QR-code e-flyer on the sign in place of paper that gets snowed on. A member of our team accompanies every showing we can, even on a $500,000 condo, because we know the property better than any agent walking in the door.
data.reach_body: Through Coldwell Banker Select and the Coldwell Banker Global Luxury network, the listing goes out to a national and international buyer base on top of our local MLS, so a home in Incline Village shows up in front of the relocating buyer in San Francisco and the family flying in from Seattle.
data.network_heading: The Network That Gets Your Home Sale-Ready.
data.network_p1: In a resort market, the best contractors are booked for months, and the right specialist is hard to find unless you already know who to call. Grant has built those relationships since 2009, and a seller inherits them the moment we sign.
data.network_p2: When a home needs work before it shows well, Grant knows who to bring in and roughly what it should cost, because he grew up on his father's job sites. Construction here runs about 50% longer and 50% more expensive than most owners budget for. Before you spend a dollar to get ready to list, we will tell you which fixes earn their money back and which to skip.
data.network_story: One of our sellers lives in Australia, and the buyer's inspector flagged the heating system. The seller skis here every winter and the heat works fine, but most plumbers won't touch a hydronic boiler. We brought in a boiler specialist, the inspector signed off, and the sale closed.
data.network_quote: We live in a resort market. It's really hard to get an electrician to come to your house. You got to take care of people. And when you treat them right, they treat you right.
data.honesty_heading: Honest Advice, Even When It Isn't What You Want to Hear.
data.honesty_p1: Grant gives sellers the truth, even when a softer answer would win the listing, because his business runs on clients who come back. One client has completed 23 transactions with our team, and several of this year's sales were homes that sat unsold with another agent last year.
data.honesty_quote: I'll always be honest, even if it's not what you want to hear.
data.honesty_p2: A plumber Grant works with inherited his father's house and had an off-market offer in hand from an agent the family knew. Grant walked the property, ran the numbers, and told him he thought we could get about half a million more. The family listed with us and sold for $550,000 more than the offer, a 46% gain, after paying the commission they had hoped to save.
data.process_heading: What Listing With Our Team Looks Like.
data.process_body: It starts with Grant at your house. He can run numbers on square footage from his desk, but your version of remodeled, his, and a buyer's are three different things, and “lake view” has several categories in our MLS, so he sees the home in person before we talk price. Then we go through the listing agreement clause by clause, so you know what a contingency does to your deal and when a buyer's earnest money becomes non-refundable. From there, it's prep, photography, the property website, the broker tour, and the market at the right moment.
data.process_promise: When offers come in, we give you the information, and you choose the route. You pick the destination, and we suggest the course to get there. Under contract, we meet the buyer's inspectors and appraiser, get contractor bids on anything they flag, protect your deposit through escrow, and attend your signing. After the keys change hands, we will handle the movers, the utilities, and whatever you left behind, or find someone who will.
data.val_heading: Start With What Your Home Is Worth.
data.val_lead: Share the address and a little about the home, and Grant will come back with a real read on value and timing, based on recent sales and the competition you would face today. There is no automated number at the end of this form and no pitch. If you like, we will set a time for Grant to walk the property.
data.val_success: Thanks. One of the team will be in touch shortly with a first read and a time to talk.
data.val_reassure: Many of the owners who call us have several properties and are still deciding how many more winters they want. A first conversation commits you to nothing, and “not this year” is a perfectly good answer.
